business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national CIPC registry; no separate sub-national company register)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch civil law heritage infused with English common law, under constitutional supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the United States of America and the Republic of South Africa for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 1997, effective 1998)
Double Taxation Relief Arrangement between South Africa and the United Kingdom (effective 2002)
Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with the Republic of Mauritius (effective 2016)
Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015 (statutory investment-protection framework superseding most legacy bilateral investment treaties)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 and the Companies Second Amendment Act 17 of 2024); General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Directive (effective 1 July 2023); CIPC Directive on the Filing of Beneficial Ownership Information (2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport (biographical page) of each director, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the country of origin, with notarization by a Notary Public in that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (South Africa is a contracting party since 1995; consular legalization applies only to issuers from non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed regulated bank or municipal utility provider, certified by a Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum of Association of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registrar (e.g., Companies House United Kingdom; BizFile Singapore)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder (issued within the last 6 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registrar or constituted authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation letter evidencing banking mandate and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing regulated bank in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized sworn declaration of beneficial ownership (consistent with CIPC beneficial ownership disclosure requirements)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commissioner of Oaths or Notary Public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory four-step screening of every director, shareholder, signatory and UBO against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the U.S. OFAC SDN List; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) the UK consolidated sanctions list; and (v) the South African FIC/Prudential Authority domestic sanctions and enforcement alerts. A Politically Exposed Person (PEP) determination is mandatory under FICA s. 28A; enhanced due diligence (EDD), including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval, applies to foreign PEPs and high-risk customers. South Africa's FATF enhanced follow-up status (grey-listing period 2023-2025) has sharply increased SARS and FIC scrutiny of new incorporations; screening results must be documented and retained in an AML file for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za) - Name Reservation Application Form CoR 9.1
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s. 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the name must be expressed in at least one of the 12 official languages of South Africa and in the script of that language. If the proposed name is in a foreign language or script, a certified translation or transliteration into English must be submitted. The corporate suffix '(Pty) Ltd' is mandatory. Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, close corporation or trademark will be rejected. CIPC Practice Notes restrict the use of hyphens, numerals and punctuation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Building Society (requires Prudential Authority prior consent)
Insurer / Insurance / Assurance (requires Prudential Authority approval)
Medical Scheme (requires Registrar of Medical Schemes consent)
Trust (restricted unless MOI establishes a trust)
Exchange / Stock Exchange (requires Financial Sector Conduct Authority consent)
University / College / Technikon (requires Department of Higher Education consent)
Chartered / Accredited / Certified (requires professional body consent)
Attorney / Advocate / Auditor (requires statutory profession regulator consent)
President / Government / Municipality / South Africa (requires ministerial consent under s. 11(3) of the Companies Act)
Reserve Bank / Treasury / SARS (statutorily prohibited tokens)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 business days from the date of the CIPC name-rejection notice (Form CoR 9.4), the applicant may file an objection or application for reconsideration through the CIPC e-Services portal. CIPC re-adjudicates and issues a fresh determination. If the name remains refused, the applicant may file an Application for Determination with the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, with further judicial review available before the High Court under s. 167(1). Legal representation is permitted at each stage; name-reservation priority is not automatically preserved during appeal, and a fresh reservation may be submitted in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions. Section 23(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requires a registered office within South Africa with a physical street address for service of process; a post-office box is insufficient. A recognized virtual-office provider that supplies a dedicated physical street address, mail handling and service-of-process acceptance satisfies this mandate. For a payroll-SaaS entity with no physical trading premises, CIPC accepts such an address; however, banks and the FIC will treat the arrangement as medium-to-high risk and may require board-meeting records, lease evidence and substance declarations. No industry-specific physical-premises licence is required for ISIC 6201.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5% annual probability of an unannounced CIPC, SARS or FIC physical inspection for a virtual-office payroll-SaaS entity). Probability increases to approximately 15-20% if the entity registers for PAYE or VAT, or processes payroll for third-party clients, owing to FATF enhanced-follow-up scrutiny of payroll data and personal information; the Information Regulator may additionally conduct POPIA compliance assessments.

Beneficial Ownership Information filing to CIPC - professional assistance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office with physical street address - 12-month term

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), sections 13, 14, 15, 19 and 66; read with the Companies Regulations, 2011 (GNR 351 of 26 April 2011)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic person established under section 185 of the Companies Act, operating the e-Services online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (standard form CoR 15.1A or bespoke MOI) filed electronically via CIPC e-Services
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Proprietary Limited (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required. The MOI determines authorised shares; subscription consideration may be cash, in-kind contribution, an undertaking, or a future service, provided the first directors resolve that the consideration is fair and adequate. Shares are subscribed at incorporation by at least one incorporator.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The subscribers' share subscription, as recorded in the Memorandum of Incorporation, be and is hereby ratified and allotted, with payment of consideration duly authorised. 2. The Company's registered office, as lodged in the Notice of Incorporation, be and is hereby adopted, and statutory records shall be maintained there under section 24 of the Companies Act. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Financial Director, and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each to hold office until successors are validly appointed. ADOPTED this ____ day of ____________ 20____.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) – e-Services name reservation module (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC e-Services portal, select 'Reservation of Company or Close Corporation Name', conduct the name availability search, and submit the prescribed name reservation request with the applicant's details. Pay the reservation fee online. The reserved name is valid for 6 months and must be used in the Notice of Incorporation before expiry, failing which the reservation lapses.
required_dossiers: Applicant's certified identity document, passport or foreign equivalent
Company Name Reservation Application details (incl. proposed name and alternate names)
Proof of e-Filing registration and payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as undesirable or confusing, CIPC issues a query; the applicant may submit alternate reserved names or a compliant name within the statutory objection period (no re-filing fee if resubmitted before expiry of the reservation window).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators appointed by the founding shareholders (no registry pre-clearance; executed documents are filed with CIPC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) adopting the standard prescribed form CoR 15.1A or a bespoke MOI meeting sections 6 to 16 of the Companies Act. The MOI sets the authorised share classes, director powers, and board quorum. Each proposed director and officer must sign a Consent to Act in the prescribed manner for filing with the Notice of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Standard or bespoke Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A)
Consent to Act as Director forms (CoR 15.1 / CoR 66.1 as applicable)
Certified copies of the identity documents of each incorporator and director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bespoke MOI contains provisions inconsistent with the Companies Act, CIPC will reject the form on registration; the promoter should procure a legal opinion and re-file a corrected MOI before the incorporation application is lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Notice of Incorporation and Registration with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC – 'Register a Company and Obtain a Registration Certificate' transaction under the e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the MOI and consent forms through the CIPC e-Services portal. Pay the prescribed registration fee electronically. Upon acceptance, CIPC issues the Company's Enterprise Number (automatically the registration number) and the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1)
Memorandum of Incorporation (final executed version)
Original or reserved name certificate (if a name was reserved)
Consent to Act forms of directors and company officer
Statement confirming registered office physical address and postal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejects the filing, the applicant receives an automatic notification stating the defect; the filing may be cured by resubmitting the corrected CoR 14.1/MOI within 20 business days from the CIPC request without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services downloads portal; statutory records maintained by the Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation and the certified MOI from the CIPC portal. The Company Secretary must establish the company's statutory records folder, minute book, and share register, and file the certificate with the MOI as the founding constitutional document.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
Memorandum of Incorporation (sealed or executed copy)
Notice of Incorporation acknowledgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated due to a system error or payment mismatch, contact the CIPC Contact Centre for a manual re-issue; the enterprise number remains valid once CIPC records reflect the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of the Inaugural Corporate Governance Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting under section 66 and the MOI (no external filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first board meeting or adopt a written board resolution in accordance with the MOI. Resolve the allotment of subscriber shares, adoption of the registered office, appointment of directors and officers, authorisation of the company bank account, appointment of the auditor or accounting officer (if required), and ratification of all pre-incorporation contracts made by the promoters.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set out in the incorporation framework)
Minute book and company seal (if adopted)
Consent to Act forms signed by directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer appointment is invalid under the MOI, the board may pass a rectifying resolution at the next meeting; if the Companies Act requires lodging of officer details with CIPC, file the CoR 30 form within the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Income Tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF and SDL with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an eFiling profile for the company and submit the compulsory registration of the company as an income tax taxpayer. Register separately for VAT if taxable turnover will exceed or already exceeds ZAR 1 million per annum; register for PAYE, UIF and Skills Development Levy (SDL) as a payroll employer if employees are or will be hired. SARS issues an Income Tax Registration Number effective from the date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified ID copies of directors
SARS eFiling business registration form (RA01 family forms)
Banking details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, reconcile the company's name and registration number against the CIPC extract; correct the eFiling profile and resubmit with the CIPC Certificate of Incorporation. A late registration penalty under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises Occupational Health and Safety, Fire and Municipal Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality (Planning and Fire Services Departments) and the Department of Employment and Labour (Health and Safety Inspectorate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a zoning certificate or municipal building consent for office-based software operations. Conduct an electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC), arrange a fire equipment inspection, obtain a fire safety certificate, and appoint a health and safety officer under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993. Register the company with the Compensation Fund for COIDA in order to hold a valid Letter of Good Standing.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
Municipal zoning certificate and building occupation certificate
Electrical Certificate of Compliance
Fire equipment inspection and certification report
Appointment letter of the health and safety officer
COIDA application and declaration of earnings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal or labour inspector issues a contravention notice, remedy the stated defect within the notice period, submit photographic proof of rectification, and apply for re-inspection; any written representation may be made to the local authority before a penalty is imposed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing licensing board applies to ISIC 6201 (software and payroll automation); the competent authority is the local Metropolitan Municipality acting under the Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act 16 of 2013 (SPLUMA) for the zoning and occupation of the office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Zoning / Occupancy Permit and Occupational Health and Safety (OHSA) Compliance Certificate; no Environmental Authorisation is required for administrative software operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and the relevant provincial environmental department delegated under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration only – office-based software services are not listed activities under Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 of the 2014 EIA Regulations; no compulsory full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to ISIC 6201 payroll automation; the premises must comply with municipal sewer discharge bylaws and urban ambient air quality standards under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004, with no industrial VOCs or process wastewater generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire department, electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC), structural load inspection by a competent person under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, and a valid Letter of Good Standing from the Compensation Fund (COIDA) for workplace injury clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - SARS eFiling portal (https://efiling.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity establishing South African operations: (1) register the external company with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); (2) apply to SARS for an Income Tax Reference Number via Form IT/TR (or eFiling 'Register a Taxpayer' functionality); (3) if taxable supplies exceed R 1,000,000 p.a., apply for VAT vendor status on Form VAT 101 (or eFiling); (4) apply for PAYE/UIF/SDL employer registration on Form EMP 101 if hiring employees. A South African (Pty) Ltd is pre-registered for income tax at incorporation and must activate its SARS profile within 60 days of incorporation by submitting notice of registration on eFiling with company documents and founder ID copies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxable at entity level on worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch rules (ss 23M-23P Income Tax Act) apply automatically, with limited elections to treat arrangements as aligned with BEPS Action 2. Available operational elections include: CFC high-tax exemption opt-out election (s 9D(2A)); VAT grouping election (s 50 VAT Act) for 50%-related companies to file as one vendor; s 24C provisions election; s 11D R&D allowance election; and employer payroll elections for retirement fund contributions and PAYE annual reconciliation (EMP 501) on SARS eFiling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: R 1,000,000 actual or expected annual taxable turnover; voluntary registration: R 50,000 annual taxable turnover; a non-resident supplying electronic services to South African residents is compulsorily registerable regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance system, continuous transaction controls (CTC), or digital stamping is currently mandated by SARS. Vendors must issue a full or abridged tax invoice containing statutory particulars (s 20 VAT Act). Electronic tax invoices (including XML/e-invoicing) are acceptable, and SARS accepts automated filing via eFiling and its API channel; a unilateral mandate for e-invoicing may be announced by SARS on notice, but none is in force for this regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (1) movable goods supplied and exported to a non-resident under s 11(1)(a) VAT Act, provided the exporter retains prescribed documentary proof and the goods leave South Africa within 90 days (or a longer SARS-approved period); (2) services supplied to a non-resident that are physically rendered outside South Africa under s 11(2)(l); (3) services connected to exported goods under s 11(2)(a)-(e). For the payroll SaaS scope, offshore SaaS and payroll automation services will qualify under s 11(2)(l) only where the recipient is a non-resident and the services are not used or consumed in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500/SAD501) lodged via SARS Customs eCSP
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill of loading evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign exchange control / RMC or General Banking Declaration)
Commercial invoice and VAT export log
Contract or sales order evidencing non-resident counterparty
Proof of receipt of payment in foreign currency
Consignment records or export permits for restricted goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without the full export evidence bundle, SARS may assess VAT at 15%, claw back input tax deductions and disallow the refund (ss 16(2)(f) and 54 VAT Act). Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, understatement penalties range from 10% (substantial non-disclosure) to 150% (intentional tax evasion) of the shortfall; deliberate fraudulent export refund schemes face a 200% penalty, interest, criminal prosecution, and personal liability of directors under s 155 TAA. SARS's customs-vat data matching with the SAD500, bank foreign-exchange records, and IRC system is the primary audit trigger.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), the statutory exchange-control regulator for South African residents. Authority derives from the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated thereunder, the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), and the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998. SARB also supervises the national payment infrastructure through the National Payment System Department (NPSD) and the Payments Association of South Africa (PASA), which operates the ACB (Automated Clearing Bureau) debit-order and EFT clearing rails. Foreign-currency allocation, force-conversion powers, and hedging approvals are administered exclusively through authorised dealers, being registered commercial banks, not through private fintech entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is fully convertible on the current account: SaaS export receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees are remittable without prior FinSurv approval, provided the resident entity moves funds through a South African authorised dealer with correct BOP purpose codes, underlying contracts/invoices, and a valid SARS tax-clearance status (TCC PIN). The capital account is restricted under a positive-list approval regime: inward direct equity investment by non-residents into a (Pty) Ltd is freely permitted without prior approval, but outward capital transfers, offshore account opening, guarantees, and foreign-currency borrowing by the resident require FinSurv approval or delegated authorised-dealer authority. Profit remittance hurdles for a payroll-SaaS exporter include: (i) dividend remittance requires a board declaration, SARS TCC PIN, BOP coding, and 20% dividend withholding tax (treaty-reduced where applicable); (ii) connected-party software licence or service payments must satisfy the s.31 transfer-pricing rules and the FinSurv royalty/fee formula (generally 0-6% of net turnover for technology licensing); (iii) shareholder loans must be documented, reported to the authorised dealer as inward loans, and must respect s.23M earnings-stripping limits (30% of tax EBITDA) and debt:equity norms; (iv) beneficial-ownership filings at CIPC and the FICA BO register must be current; and (v) all export earnings must be repatriated to South Africa within the prescribed timeline—they cannot be accumulated in offshore EMIs or bank accounts without FinSurv approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since 1 January 2021, the historical mandatory 10% surrender of export proceeds to the SARB has been abolished; the statutory conversion ratio for export receipts is now 0%. The general timeline is that services-export proceeds (including SaaS subscription revenue) must be received in South Africa within 180 days of the invoice date, extendable to 360 days by an authorised dealer on application; goods-export proceeds must be received within 180 days of shipment. Upon inward receipt, funds must be converted to ZAR within 30 days unless the exporter maintains an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with a South African authorised dealer permitting retention in USD/EUR. For a payroll-SaaS platform invoicing global clients in foreign currency, each inward MT103 credit must be matched to a signed SaaS agreement and invoice, coded under the SARB BOP computer-services category, and retained for five years in the FinSurv/SARS compliance file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR current account plus USD/EUR Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for export-proceeds retention; segregated client-funds escrow structure available under PASA approval

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR current account plus USD/EUR FCA and integrated treasury FX/forward desk via Rand Merchant Bank division
Operational ZAR current account plus USD FCA with corporate e-accounting and capital-receipt documentation workflows
Operational ZAR current account plus USD/EUR FCA; ACB debit-order origination and payroll-industry cash-management suite
Operational ZAR account plus specialised treasury, escrow, and structured FX-hedging facilities; suited to medium-sized corporate sponsors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury operations. A South African resident (Pty) Ltd may not maintain undisclosed offshore balances with non-authorised fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, or EU/UK EMI shells) because such accounts violate the Exchange Control Regulations and the compulsory repatriation/retention framework—only FinSurv or an authorised dealer may approve an offshore facility. Offshore EMIs are not authorised dealers, do not participate in SARB reporting, and cannot operate ACB debit-order or SAMOS settlement rails. Their permissible role is limited to peripheral client-side collection gateways, provided funds are swept immediately into the South African bank account of the entity without creating an overnight offshore balance. Every payroll disbursement or vendor settlement for the SaaS operation must clear through a PASA-member sponsored account and a licensed authorised dealer, with BOP reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA does not impose a universal statutory requirement for every director to appear physically at a branch, but every accountable institution must positively verify the identity of directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners using original or certified/apostilled documentation. In practice, the South African tier-1 banks require either (i) a physical appointment at a corporate banking branch for at least one locally resident authorised signatory, supported by video interviews for all non-resident directors, or (ii) a fully remote flow with notarised/apostilled passports, live facial-recognition checks, a foreign-bank reference letter, and electronic board-resolution verification. For a Medium_Risk_Enhanced payroll-SaaS profile, SA banks will additionally demand a screening call with the AML compliance officer and the UBOs; full remote opening with zero physical footprint is technically available at FNB and Nedbank for lower-risk entities, but a single Johannesburg signing session on day one materially shortens enhanced-due-diligence timelines and avoids account-activation delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with no South African footprint and multiple intermediate holding layers obscuring the ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate-chain organogram to natural-person UBOs; certified ID/passport copies of each UBO; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register extract as amended by the General Laws Amendment Act 2023; 12-month foreign-bank statements and banker's references; notarised power of attorney for the local authorised signatory; completed UN/EU/OFAC/HM Treasury sanctions and PEP screening results; and a FICA-compliant Risk and Compliance Programme (RCP) naming the appointed AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll-SaaS platform perceived as unlicensed money remittance or escrow because it touches employee salary flows and may be misclassified as a deposit-taking or payment intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal legal opinion confirming pure-software classification with no custody, no deposit-taking, and no proprietary payment-system participation; sponsored PASA/ACB debit-order agreement showing client funds remain at all times in the client's own bank account; flow-of-funds diagram; ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II attestations; FICA registration certificate; AML/CFT programme, staff training logs, and independent compliance-review report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound SWIFT MT103 credits from numerous lower-income or high-risk jurisdictions without matching export or subscription documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS subscription agreements and order forms per corporate client; itemised invoices and unique payment references; IFRS 15 revenue-recognition schedule; monthly bank-to-FX reconciliation and BOP purpose-code mapping; sanctions-screening logs; IP-geolocation and device-log evidence demonstrating bona fide non-resident end users; and transfer-pricing documentation for any connected-party income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder loans followed by rapid dividend or interest repatriation, indicating round-tripping, thin-capitalisation, or earnings-stripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed inward-loan agreement reported to the authorised dealer/FinSurv in the inward-loan register; board minutes evidencing genuine commercial purpose; SARS tax-clearance PIN; s.23M calculation capped at 30% of tax EBITDA; arm's-length interest-rate benchmark; dividend declaration and SARB BOP outward-dividend coding; proof of 20% dividend-WHT payment to SARS (or treaty-rate annex); and a board-approved cash-flow forecast proving the dividend does not simply recycle the inward loan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Connected-party licence, royalty, or management fees from the foreign parent exceeding industry norms or lacking economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing master file and South African local file under s.31 of the Income Tax Act; benchmark study confirming royalty/licensing within FinSurv's 0-6% of net turnover formula for software technology; executed service-level agreements and time records for intra-group support; resale-price-margin evidence for embedded payroll software; SARS corporate-income-tax and CbC-reporting extracts; and independent IP valuation if any licence buy-in or asset transfer is contemplated.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors wire USD/EUR via SWIFT MT103 (gpi) to the company's USD/EUR FCA or directly to the ZAR operating account at the selected South African authorised dealer. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'INW/EQ - share subscription - ZA_PTY_LTD - allotment [date]' and reference the SARB BOPDIR purpose code for inward direct investment in equity capital; no FinSurv pre-approval is required for inward ordinary shares in a software (Pty) Ltd. The bank will treat the credit as conditionally cleared until the company files: (i) board resolution allotting the shares; (ii) signed share certificates; (iii) CIPC notice and amended MOI/CoR proof; (iv) SARS tax-status confirmation; (v) inward-investment declaration; and (vi) updated FICA/CIPC beneficial-ownership records. Upon verification, funds convert to cleared ZAR or remain in an approved FCA; the allotment must then be lodged at CIPC and the capital registered with the authorised dealer so that future dividends, interest, and disinvestment proceeds are freely remittable. If the injection is instead structured as a shareholder loan, the loan must be documented, reported as an inward loan, and its interest/repayment will require SARS tax clearance, BOP coding, and compliance with s.23M and debt:equity limits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Vendor, infrastructure, and subcontractor payments are executed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV through the authorised dealer with underlying invoice/contract evidence and BOP service codes (e.g., computer and information services, business services). Commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 are available for physical hardware or delivery-guaranteed software projects, but recurring SaaS licensing is normally settled open-account via MT103. The payroll automation model also requires the South African ACB direct-debit (ACH) rail: the company, or its PASA-sponsored payment partner, originates debit orders from local client bank accounts, then settles any foreign net obligation by MT103 through the authorised dealer. Outbound current-account payments in sensitive categories—royalties, connected-party services, or transactions exceeding the authorised dealer's delegated threshold—require FinSurv pre-approval, SARS tax-clearance, and a royalty/service agreement. Outbound dividends to the non-resident shareholder are remitted by MT103 with BOP outward-dividend coding, the dividend declaration, SARS TCC PIN, 20% dividend-WHT proof (or treaty-rate annex), and must originate solely from the South African banking book; no routing through offshore EMIs or third-country conduits is permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) in USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR, with a maximum tenor of 12 months, against committed or highly probable SaaS receivables and vendor payables, executed exclusively through a South African authorised dealer.
FX rollovers and tom-next swaps on approved Foreign Currency Account balances for short-dated cash-flow alignment.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-term offshore shareholder loans or preference-share liabilities.
Vanilla OTC currency options (USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR calls and puts) on a covered basis with premium paid up front; naked option writing is prohibited.
Exchange-traded USD/ZAR futures and options on the JSE (Safex) for centrally cleared, collateral-efficient hedging.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/ZAR offshore—permissible only with specific FinSurv approval and demonstrable underlying offshore exposure; generally disfavoured for South African resident corporates because the ZAR is deliverable and the onshore FEC market is the compliant alternative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each annual anniversary of incorporation date; no extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs monthly administrative penalty; persistent non-filing leads to compulsory deregistration after publication of final notice in the Government Gazette

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed together with the Annual Return or, if there is no change, before the Annual Return deadline; changes must be reported within 10 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain the Beneficial Ownership Register is an administrative offence with fines up to ZAR 250,000 against the company and personal liability for directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent external audit mandatory for all public or state-owned companies and for any private company with a Public Interest Score (PIS) of 350 or more; an independent review is required when PIS is between 100 and 349
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs, as permitted by the Companies Act 71 of 2008; local GAAP is not independently published for South African companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and submit an annual confirmation naming any individual holding 5% or more of issued shares, voting rights, or power of control; each transfer of beneficial ownership triggers an update within 10 business days, and the annual confirmation must accompany the CIPC Annual Return
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholder and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; formerly 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; SBC progressive rates apply for qualifying Pty Ltd (0%/7%/21%/27% on taxable income up to ZAR 550,000); s11D R&D super-deduction (150%); s12B renewable-energy 100% first-year allowance; s12E SBC accelerated manufacturing allowances; s12H learnership allowances; foreign tax credits under s6quat.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward of assessed losses (s20 ITA) subject to s20A anti-trafficking rules; no fixed 5-year limitation — the schema default of 5 is corrected to reflect South African law.
